headline: Post-transcriptional RNA control profiled across human tissues, genomes and proteomes
label: Post Transcriptional Rna Regulation
summary: Human atlases, a diploid reference genome, and NMD escape modeling extend analysis of RNA regulation across genes, organs, and proteomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is post-transcriptional control of RNA fate, measured with large-scale sequencing and functional assays. NMDetective-AI trains a genomic language model on allele-specific premature termination codon expression from human cohorts and pairs it with deep mutational scanning, framing NMD escape as graded and gene-dependent rather than all-or-none. A total RNA-seq atlas across 22 human organs profiles non-coding RNAs and subcellular localization, while GC3 codon bias and tRNA-modification indices are linked to tissue and cancer proteomes. Adjacent work extends the regulatory axis to genome architecture: a telomere-to-telomere diploid H9 reference annotates segmental duplications, NOTCH2NL duplications are examined for regulatory features, and promoter methylomes across 82 vertebrate assemblies show conserved TSS hypomethylation. These studies do not converge on a single method.
